findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Acknowledge that placing the ADF encode in acli_cli_ops.add_comment affects EVERY Cloud add_comment caller (including the illegal-transition machine-comment fallback at dispatch_one.py:644) and state that this broader wire-shape change is intended/benign.
evidence: Grep for `.add_comment(` finds a THIRD source-side call: dispatch_one.py:644 `cast("SupportsComments", client).add_comment(issue_key, comment)` — the 400-illegal-transition machine-comment fallback ('local status changed to <status>').
The encode is added inside the shared primitive acli_cli_ops.add_comment (:469), so every Cloud caller of add_comment is affected, not only the two named sync sites.
The plan's ID-capture scope correctly excludes :644 (it has no local_comment_key), but the encode blast-radius on that path is not acknowledged.
findings.finding: The plan frames comment enactment as exactly 'two sites' (dispatch_one.py:418 create, dispatch_apply_phases.py:165 update) and places the Cloud ADF encode inside the SHARED transport primitive acli_cli_ops.add_comment, but does not enumerate that this changes ALL Cloud add_comment callers — including a third add_comment call site, the illegal-transition machine-comment fallback at dispatch_one.py:644 — whose bodies would then also be ADF-encoded.
findings.location: Approach §1a ('both enacting sites currently DISCARD it: dispatch_one.py:418 ... dispatch_apply_phases.py:165'); Scope (acli_cli_ops.py add_comment :469)
scenarios: An illegal-transition update triggers the :644 fallback comment; after the change its plain 'local status changed to X' body is now ADF-encoded on Cloud — a behavioral change the plan never mentions.
Any other Cloud add_comment invocation silently begins shipping ADF.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a Scope note enumerating dispatch_one.py:644 as an incidentally-affected Cloud add_comment caller and confirm the machine-comment fallback body renders correctly (or scope the encode to only the sync enactment sites rather than the shared primitive).

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Pin the Cloud comment encode to ONE layer: state whether the ADF serialize happens in the differ (via the resolved RichTextCodec.to_wire) or in acli_cli_ops.add_comment (via the module-local _text_to_adf mirroring acli.py:205), and if the latter, explain how/whether the codec reaches the transport (or that it uses _text_to_adf, not to_wire).
evidence: acli_cli_ops.add_comment (:469-492) takes only (jira_key, body, *, acli_cmd); it does NOT receive or import a RichTextCodec instance.
The description path the plan cites as the mirror (acli.py:205) uses the module-level `_text_to_adf` (imported at acli.py:60 / acli_cli_ops.py:32), NOT codec.to_wire.
AAdfCodec lives in adapters/jira/rich_text_codec.py; jira_family/rich_text.py forbids importing from adapters/jira, and the transport primitive has no codec handle threaded to it.

Plan quote: '_map_comments_for_create/_decorate_outbound_comment' render via to_wire, but Scope also puts the encode 'add the Cloud comment-body encode step (--body json.dumps(to_wire(body)))' inside acli_cli_ops.add_comment.
findings.finding: The Cloud comment-body encode step's LOCATION is specified inconsistently: the plan says render via RichTextCodec.to_wire in the differ-layer builders (_map_comments_for_create/_decorate_outbound_comment) yet ALSO says to add `--body json.dumps(to_wire(body))` inside the transport primitive acli_cli_ops.add_comment, which holds no RichTextCodec and whose real mirror of acli.py:205 is the module-local _text_to_adf import, not the codec to_wire.
findings.location: Approach §2 + Scope (acli_cli_ops.py add_comment :469); Approach §2 ("rendered through the SAME RichTextCodec.to_wire seam ... applied in _map_comments_for_create/_decorate_outbound_comment")
scenarios: Implementer wires codec.to_wire into acli_cli_ops.add_comment and finds no codec is available at the transport layer; or double-encodes (renders in the differ AND again in the transport).
The differ-layer decorate/render and the transport-layer encode disagree on the wire shape (dict vs str vs already-serialized), producing malformed ADF.
findings.suggested_fix: Either (a) render+serialize once in the differ layer (codec-aware) and leave acli_cli_ops.add_comment accepting an already-encoded body, or (b) mirror acli.py:205 exactly by using the transport's own `_text_to_adf` (acli_cli_ops.py:32) as `json.dumps(_text_to_adf(body))` and drop the `to_wire` phrasing at that site.

evidence: 1 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State explicitly that pre-existing (already-synced, pre-map) comments are protected on the first post-deploy pass by the retained body-equality secondary skip, and add/extend an AC proving no re-post for a comment present on Jira with no map entry AND no jira_comment_id.
evidence: 'the demoted body-equality guard (§1b) still catches a comment already on Jira should any single map write be lost' — framed as crash-durability, not as the migration bridge for pre-existing comments
New map is 'added once' per comment; pre-existing comments never had a create pass under this code so no entry exists for them
An already-synced outbound-origin comment carries no jira_comment_id (that field is inbound-origin only, _processors.py:354-356)
findings.finding: The plan does not explicitly address how comments that were ALREADY synced before this change (already on Jira, with no entry in the new outbound ID map and — being outbound-origin — no jira_comment_id field) are handled on the first reconcile pass after deploy. On that first pass the PRIMARY guard (ID map) will miss them and they rely entirely on the DEMOTED body-equality secondary skip to avoid a duplicate re-post.
scenarios: First reconcile pass after this story deploys, on a binding that already mirrored comments under the old body-equality regime
findings.suggested_fix: Add a sentence to §1b naming the pre-existing-comment migration case (not just the crash case), and generalize test_comment_crash_between_add_and_map_save_no_duplicate — or add a sibling AC — to cover the no-map-entry pre-existing comment under the flipped codec key.

findings.finding: The outbound differ loses its only loop-breaker for inbound-origin comments: removing the body-equality membership test and replacing it solely with the outbound map (which has no entry for inbound-origin comments) causes every inbound-mirrored comment to be re-pushed to Jira as a duplicate.
findings.location: Approach §1b / Scope: outbound_comments.py (_diff_comments :143 keyed by map instead of body)
findings.suggested_fix: In the outbound differ, skip a local comment when EITHER (a) its local HLC key is already a key in the outbound map, OR (b) it carries a `jira_comment_id` field (inbound-origin). Add an AC asserting an inbound-origin comment (has `jira_comment_id`, no map entry) is not re-pushed outbound (extend test_comment_bidirectional_identity_no_double_sync to cover exactly this local-comment shape).

findings.finding: The codec-injection flip attributes the change solely to `outbound_comments.py` (`_diff_comments`'s `_resolve_codec` default), but the real production injection is made by the CALLER via the `codec=` argument. `_diff_comments`'s sole production call site — `compute_outbound_mutations` at `outbound_differ.py:741` — passes NO `codec=` today (so it defaults to `_IdentityCodec`). Flipping the injection to the real `RichTextCodec` requires editing `outbound_differ.py:741`, which is absent from the plan's Scope file list. This is confirmed by the a32a ticket's own completion note: 'nothing wires a real codec into compute_outbound_mutations ... injecting the real codec is a one-line change.' Flipping the default inside `outbound_comments._resolve_codec` instead would silently alter every other caller — including a32a's baseline test that pins identity behavior when no codec is injected.
findings.location: Scope: `outbound_comments.py` — 'flip the `_diff_comments` a32a codec injection (`_resolve_codec`) from `_IdentityCodec` to the real `RichTextCodec`'
findings.suggested_fix: In Scope, add `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_differ.py` — pass the real `RichTextCodec` into the `_diff_comments(...)` call at `:741` (inside `compute_outbound_mutations`) so the production comment-diff routes the local dedup key through `normalize_outbound`; leave `outbound_comments._resolve_codec`'s `_IdentityCodec` default intact so a32a's no-codec baseline tests stay green.

findings.finding: The Scope locates the codec-injection flip in outbound_comments.py (_resolve_codec), but the actual injection is made by the caller via the codec= argument. _diff_comments's sole production caller is _compute_outbound_update_mutation at outbound_differ.py:741 (passes no codec), and the create-path renderer _map_comments_for_create is called at outbound_differ.py:624 with only `ticket`. outbound_differ.py is absent from Scope/file_impact, so the real patch site for both 'flip to real RichTextCodec' and 'render create bodies via to_wire' is unenumerated.
findings.location: Scope — outbound_comments.py bullet: 'flip the `_diff_comments` a32a codec injection (`_resolve_codec`) from `_IdentityCodec` to the real `RichTextCodec`'; AC line 5
findings.suggested_fix: List src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_differ.py in Scope: pass the deployment's RichTextCodec as codec= at _diff_comments (:741) and thread it into _map_comments_for_create (:624) so both outbound comment call sites use the real rendering codec.

findings.finding: The create-path function the plan repeatedly names `_create_one` (Approach 1a(ii) and AC2) does not exist under that name; the actual function receiving `binding_store` at `dispatch_one.py:154` is `create_one` (no leading underscore).
findings.suggested_fix: Replace both occurrences of `_create_one` with `create_one` (the actual function name at dispatch_one.py:147).

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the RETIRE path for the comment-ID map (e.g. it is removed with the rest of the binding state on binding teardown) so the shared-state lifecycle is complete.
evidence: 'persistent per-binding comment-ID map local_comment_key → jira_id ... (change-gated, append-only, fixed-shape entry)'
No mention of map removal on binding retirement / ticket deletion anywhere in Scope or Approach
findings.finding: The new persistent per-binding comment-ID map has a well-specified CREATE/UPDATE/CONSUME lifecycle but no described RETIRE/cleanup path: it is append-only (one entry per comment, never removed), and the plan does not say what happens to the map when the binding itself is torn down or the mirrored ticket is deleted.
scenarios: A binding is deleted or a ticket is unmirrored — the per-binding comment-ID map's cleanup is undefined
findings.suggested_fix: Add a note that the comment-ID map lives inside the binding state and is removed atomically when the binding is retired (citing the existing binding-state teardown path), confirming no separate cleanup is needed.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the local comment map key collision-proof independent of HLC fallback modes (e.g. compose the HLC timestamp with the COMMENT event's `uuid`, already on the event at `_processors.py`), or state explicitly why a `REBAR_HLC=0`/`physical_now()` timestamp tie is out of scope — the plan's 'unique, monotonic' claim does not hold under the documented HLC fallback paths (`hlc.py:143-160`) and a tie silently drops a distinct-body comment.
evidence: Plan §1: 'whose HLC timestamp (unique, monotonic; already threaded onto the compiled comment entry at reducer/_processors.py:349) is the stable local comment identity — nothing else on the entry (body/author/source_*) is collision-proof once body-equality is abandoned.'
hlc.py:143-150 — 'With the clock disabled (REBAR_HLC=0) this is exactly physical_now() — today's time.time_ns() behavior'; the +1 monotonic floor is only applied in the enabled path.
hlc.py:158-160 — 'Any error in the enabled path falls back to physical_now()' with no +1 floor, so two COMMENT events on one ticket within the same ns tick can tie.

Mechanism consequence: with a tied key, the outbound differ (Approach §1b(a)) sees the second comment's local key 'already in the map' and skips CREATE — the demoted body-equality fallback (§1b) only catches IDENTICAL bodies, so a distinct-body second comment is never posted (silent data loss), not a duplicate.
findings.finding: The plan designates the COMMENT event's HLC timestamp as the sole, 'collision-proof' local map key, but under the documented HLC fallback modes the timestamp is not guaranteed unique, and a key collision silently DROPS a distinct-body new comment (never posts it to Jira) rather than duplicating it.
findings.location: Approach §1 ('HLC timestamp (unique, monotonic; …) is the stable local comment identity — nothing else on the entry … is collision-proof'); reducer/_processors.py:350; binding_store map key
scenarios: A repo running with REBAR_HLC=0 (documented kill-switch) creates two rebar comments with different text in the same process tick — the second never syncs to Jira.
An HLC tick error falls back to physical_now(); two near-simultaneous COMMENT events collide and one comment's id-map entry overwrites the other, dropping one comment from outbound sync.
findings.suggested_fix: Key the map on a composite that stays unique under the fallback clock — e.g. the COMMENT event's `uuid` (available on the event) alone, or `(timestamp, uuid)` — surfaced onto the compiled comment entry alongside `timestamp`, so two same-ns comments never collide; then thread that composite key as `local_comment_key`.
